text:
alex: quick run of the head-to-head micro-harness (streaming vs non-streaming) on the rtx-32 farm. noticed streaming tail is worse for long-prefix sessions (>1k tokens). putting raw numbers below.
priya: can you paste the perf counters and which kernels were picked?
alex: pasted below. harness used kernel selection heuristics (auto) and our new batching cap from last week.

```
perf_summary:
kernel_selected: attn_opt_v2
kernel_switch_ratio: 0.42
avg_continuous_batch_streaming: 8.3
avg_batch_nonstreaming: 12.9
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78
kv_evictions_per_min: 230
p99_latency_streaming: 320ms
p99_latency_nonstreaming: 262ms
gpu_util_streaming: 63%
gpu_util_nonstreaming: 81%
cpu_stall_cycles: 14%
```

max: interesting — kernel_switch_ratio ~0.42 implies we're hitting the fallback path frequently (opt_v2 -> generic) as seq len grows. that can cost a lot in streaming where we expect continuous KV reuse.
priya: kv_evictions 230/min seems high. are we trimming KV aggressively for streaming? that would explain re-warm + switch thrash.
emily: last week's batching cap MR (PR #4123) lowered the target for streaming to 8 when client backpressure observed. maybe combined effect: smaller batches + kernel switches + KV churn -> poor throughput/latency.

alex: repro command I used in case someone wants to run locally:
```
./harness \
  --mode streaming \
  --workload sessions/long_prefix_1k.json \
  --override-kernel auto \
  --batch-target 16 \
  --kv-lifespan 45 \
  --duration 600
```

alex: when I forced the kernel to attn_opt_v1 (older but more stable for large seq) the p99 dropped ~15% and gpu util went up. so kernel selection + small batch sizes are probably the combo killing streaming performance.
max: can you also run with FORCE_KERNEL=attn_opt_v2_nofallback ? that would prove fallback cost.
alex: yep will run, queued it now.
perf-bot: smoke-run queued by alex at 1795246105 :running_small: ; results will post when done.

priya: long-term fix options I see:
- make kernel selection aware of streaming prefix reuse (avoid fallback if KV reuse high)
- relax the streaming batch cap when GPU util < 70% and kv_hit_rate > 0.7
- increase kv-lifespan or change eviction policy to LRU-with-prefetch for streaming sessions

emily: +1 to a temporary triage: pin kernel for problematic experiments and revert batching cap for streaming until we land a smarter heuristic.

alex: will open a ticket with data + reproducer (assign to eng-runtime). adding short checklist in the ticket: attach flamegraph, perf counters, raw harness command, and run with FORCE_KERNEL variations.
max: tag me on the ticket. i'll try an instrumentation patch to surface kernel switch cause (shape mismatch vs seq len vs chunk boundary).

alex: final note — this only showed up on longer prefix traces; short sessions are still fine. suggests it's an interaction between chunk boundary alignment and kernel shape selection, not a pure batching bug.
priya: good call. thanks all — keep updates in thread.
